Shri Amit Raval, learned counsel for the respondent/Stat  ORDER 1.

These are the first application under Section 482 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023/Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail filed by both the applicants Mrs. Swapnil Purohit in MCRC.No.2435/2025 and applicant-Mr. Shirish Satarkar in MCRC.No.2423/2025.
2.

This order shall govern the disposal of MCRC.No.2435/2025 and MCRC.No.2423/2025, as both the bail applications have, arisen out of the same crime No.48/2024.
3.

The applicants are apprehending their arrest in connection with & Crime No.48/2024 registered at Police Station Economic Offence Wing, District Indore for offence punishable under Sections 420,467,468,471,120-B of the IPC and Section 7 of the Prevention of Corruption Act of 1988.

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience facts as narrated in MCRC.No.2435/2025 are being taken into consideration.

5. The allegation against the applicant-Mrs. Swapnil Purohit (MCRC.No.2435/2025) is that she was the Manager in the Bank of Baroda, branch Sukhaliya, Indore wherein a huge embezzlement of Rs.348.31-Lakhs has taken place, whereby, the aforesaid amount was lent to the borrowers in conspiracy with other co-accused persons including the bank employees and chartered accountants etc., and subsequently, it was found that the borrower firm itself was a fake identity, and the documents relating to collateral security was also found to be forged.

6. Shri Vivek Singh, learned senior counsel for the applicant has submitted that the period during which the amount was lent to the borrowers was in the year 2014, whereas the FIR has been lodged on 12.12.2024, against 38 persons.

It is submitted that the main allegations are against the co-accused Mukesh Pandya, who was the then Branch Manager in the said bank, branch at Sukhaliya, and he was responsible for physical verification of the documents, and the assets of the borrowers, whereas the applicant had signed as the co- signatory of the documents, only on the basis of documents verified by the co-accused Mukesh Pandya.
&
7.

It is further submitted that the applicant is a woman aged 48 years, and has no criminal antecedents, and if arrested, an irreparable injury shall be caused to her reputation as also to the reputation of her family.

It is also submitted that otherwise also the applicant had cooperated during the investigation as is also apparent from her statement given to the investigating officer during the course of investigation, and thus, her custodial investigation is not required.

8. Shri Singh, has also submitted that the applicant- Shirish Satarkar(MCRC.No.2423/2023) is a retired (Joint Manager) employee of the Bank, and is aged 66 years, and he has also cooperated in the investigation, and has already given his statement to the police.
and his arrest would gravely affect his retired life as there is no allegation that the applicant had also verified the documents or the assets of the borrowers.

9. Counsel for the respondent/state on the other hand has opposed the prayer, and it is submitted that looking to the seriousness of the offence, and the huge amount involved in embezzlement, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out as the custodial interrogation of the applicants would be necessary.
10. Heard.

Having heard the rival submissions, and on perusal of the case diary, and also on a query made to counsel for the respondents, it is found that statements of both the applicants were recorded during the investigation, and the fact that the main allegations are against the co-accused Mukesh Pandya, this Court is of the considered opinion that the custodial interrogation of the applicants are not required.

sentences.text: Accordingly, without commenting upon the merits of the case, both the applications are allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, both the applicants Mrs. Swapnil Purohit in MCRC.No.2435/2025 and applicant-Mr. Shirish Satarkar in MCRC.No.2423/2025 shall be released on bail, upon their executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/-(rupees twenty five thousand only) each and furnishing one solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
The applicants shall make themselves available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.

They shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
12. MCRC.No.2435/2025 and MCRC.No.2423/2025 stands allowed and disposed of.

( SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE das Mrs Swapnil Purohit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153898108/
